TUN.headline: Headline inflation mixes free-price and administered-price systems.
TUN.dek: Tunisia's room separates the headline CPI from the institutional price system behind it. INS publishes the index; the Central Bank uses it for policy; administered and subsidized prices mean some components do not behave like market-clearing prices.

measurement_notes.question: Does headline CPI mean every price is freely determined?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Tunisia has administered and subsidized prices. Headline CPI measures the observed basket, but component dynamics can reflect policy decisions as well as market conditions.

measurement_notes.question: Is the INS ex-food-and-energy measure automatically the same as any 'core inflation' series?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Core measures are definition-dependent. The room preserves the exact exclusion rule rather than standardizing the label by assumption.

measurement_notes.question: Can a policy-rate change be interpreted without the inflation measure the BCT is reacting to?
measurement_notes.answer: Not cleanly. The room pairs dated BCT decisions with the official INS price release vintage available at the time.

measurement_notes.question: Does a stable regulated price mean underlying scarcity disappeared?
measurement_notes.answer: Not necessarily. Administered prices can suppress or delay pass-through, so price stability in a component may reflect policy architecture rather than unconstrained market balance.

measurement_notes.question: Can French and Arabic official releases be merged only by translated titles?
measurement_notes.answer: No. The Lab keeps source-language labels and publication metadata so similarly translated series are not accidentally collapsed.

ledger.revised: No revision observed in source consulted

findings.title: Tunisia's headline inflation rate is partly a map of price institutions.
findings.body: The CPI combines market-priced items with goods and services affected by administered prices and subsidies. The same 5.4% headline can therefore contain components operating under very different price-setting regimes.
findings.why: Comparing component inflation without price-setting metadata can misread policy-controlled stability as market stability.

findings.title: The core label needs a formula, not a nickname.
findings.body: INS reports an inflation measure excluding food products and energy. The Lab records that exact exclusion rather than treating every 'core' series as definitionally interchangeable across countries.
findings.why: Cross-country core-inflation charts often hide materially different exclusion rules.

LBN.headline: A Lebanese economic number can change meaning when its currency conversion vintage changes.

measurement_notes.question: If an LBP series rises, did its USD value rise?
measurement_notes.answer: Not necessarily. In a large currency revaluation environment, nominal LBP growth and USD-equivalent growth can have opposite signs. Every conversion needs a dated exchange-rate vintage.

measurement_notes.question: Which dollar rate?
measurement_notes.answer: The room distinguishes the BDL official rate from any market or historical parallel rate. A generic 'USD/LBP' field is not sufficient provenance.

measurement_notes.question: Can pre-change and post-change LBP series be graphed without denomination notes?
measurement_notes.answer: They can be graphed, but interpretation can be badly misleading. Currency-unit changes, accounting restatements and exchange-rate regime changes must travel with the series.

measurement_notes.question: Can a current USD conversion be applied retrospectively to historical local-currency values?
measurement_notes.answer: Only if the research question explicitly asks for constant-current-rate conversion. It cannot be presented as what the historical value was worth at the time.

measurement_notes.question: Why withhold a fresh unemployment number?
measurement_notes.answer: Freshness is part of evidence quality. An older survey result should not be made to look current merely because no newer official observation is easy to retrieve.

findings.title: In Lebanon, denomination can dominate the story before economics even begins.
findings.body: A nominal LBP series, a USD-converted series and a price-deflated real series answer different questions. The room prohibits silent conversion because exchange-rate choice can change both magnitude and apparent trend.
findings.why: Many apparent Lebanese 'growth' or 'collapse' comparisons are partly unit-selection problems.

findings.title: The official exchange-rate series is evidence, not a universal conversion key.
findings.body: BDL's official USD/LBP rate is a defined official series. It should not be silently substituted for market-price questions or used retrospectively without stating the conversion convention.
findings.why: Exchange-rate provenance belongs in every converted observation, particularly through regime changes.

measurement_notes.question: Is 1,310 IQD/USD 'the Iraqi exchange rate'?
measurement_notes.answer: It is the current official CBI rate displayed in the room baseline. A market or street rate is a different object and must be sourced separately.

measurement_notes.question: Can the official-market gap be calculated from an official-rate page alone?
measurement_notes.answer: No. A premium needs a contemporaneous market-rate source, matching timestamp and a documented formula.

measurement_notes.question: Which Iraqi interest rate?
measurement_notes.answer: The CBI policy rate is not interchangeable with bank lending rates, deposit rates or rates attached to other facilities. Instrument identity is mandatory.

measurement_notes.question: Does headline GDP growth describe non-oil domestic conditions?
measurement_notes.answer: Not necessarily. Oil output, prices and export conditions can dominate aggregate movements. Oil and non-oil components should be separated where official accounts permit.

measurement_notes.question: Can annual fiscal performance be read without oil-price context?
measurement_notes.answer: Not safely. Oil revenue exposure makes commodity price, export volume and fiscal realization part of the provenance chain for interpretation.

findings.title: The official exchange rate does not measure the exchange-rate premium.
findings.body: The CBI currently displays an official rate of 1,310 IQD per USD. Any statement about a parallel-market premium requires a second contemporaneous market observation; the official rate alone cannot supply it.
findings.why: A common Iraq data error is to collapse an administered official rate and a market-gap question into one field.

findings.title: 'The interest rate' is not a valid Iraqi monetary variable name.
findings.body: The CBI policy rate is one instrument. Lending, deposit and other financial rates measure different prices and transmission channels.
findings.why: Instrument metadata is necessary before time-series or cross-country comparison.

measurement_notes.question: Is a CPI reading of 110 '10% inflation'?
measurement_notes.answer: No. An index level and a growth rate are different objects. Inflation requires a comparison across periods under a defined formula.

measurement_notes.question: Which QCB rate?
measurement_notes.answer: QCB publishes distinct deposit, lending and repo rates. Cross-country policy comparisons should identify the instrument instead of selecting whichever rate is easiest to find.

measurement_notes.question: Can the latest GDP history be treated as what analysts knew at the first release date?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Quarterly accounts may be revised. The ledger distinguishes first estimate, later revision and current vintage.

measurement_notes.question: Does a fixed QAR/USD regime make monetary policy identical to the US?
measurement_notes.answer: No. The peg is a major constraint and transmission channel, but domestic liquidity operations, banking conditions and instrument settings remain distinct evidence.

measurement_notes.question: Can hydrocarbon and non-hydrocarbon growth be collapsed?
measurement_notes.answer: They can be aggregated for total GDP, but sector decomposition is essential for interpreting domestic demand versus energy-sector movements.

findings.title: Qatar has multiple policy rates; 'the QCB rate' is under-specified.
findings.body: The room baseline separately records the QCB deposit, lending and repo rates. They are distinct instruments with different roles.
findings.why: Instrument ambiguity can create fake cross-country rate gaps or false event-study timing.

findings.title: GDP revision is part of the data-generating process, not clerical noise.
findings.body: The Lab stores first estimates separately from later national-account vintages instead of overwriting history with the newest table.
findings.why: This enables a genuine 'what was knowable?' reconstruction for forecasting and policy analysis.

measurement_notes.question: Does the USD peg imply Oman simply copies every US rate move?
measurement_notes.answer: The peg creates a strong monetary constraint and transmission channel, but domestic facilities, liquidity conditions and bank balance sheets still matter. Pass-through is an empirical question.

measurement_notes.question: Omani unemployment or total unemployment?
measurement_notes.answer: Nationality is a core labour-market perimeter in Oman. Omani, expatriate and total measures should not be collapsed.

measurement_notes.question: Survey employment or administrative employment?
measurement_notes.answer: Administrative worker counts and household labour status answer different questions. Source type is part of the variable definition.

measurement_notes.question: Total GDP or non-oil activity?
measurement_notes.answer: Hydrocarbon production can materially move total output. Non-oil components are needed for domestic-demand interpretation.

measurement_notes.question: Can a fixed exchange rate be treated as a constant nominal conversion without a date?
measurement_notes.answer: The regime is fixed, but published official rates and accounting conventions still need source and date metadata.

findings.title: The peg is a constraint, not a complete monetary model.
findings.body: Oman's fixed exchange arrangement makes US monetary conditions highly relevant, but domestic liquidity facilities, bank funding and credit conditions remain separate transmission objects.
findings.why: Treating peg economies as mechanical copies can erase the very channels a policy or banking analysis needs to study.

findings.title: Nationality belongs in the labour variable name.
findings.body: Oman's labour system distinguishes Omani and expatriate employment structures. A total rate or count can conceal a materially different national labour-market story.
findings.why: Same label, different perimeter is especially important in Gulf labour statistics.

measurement_notes.question: If a labour figure is still on an official portal, is it a 2026 labour figure?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Publication availability and reference-period freshness are different metadata fields. The room never carries an older observation forward without its date.

measurement_notes.question: Survey unemployment or administrative employment?
measurement_notes.answer: They are different constructs. LMRA administrative worker records and survey-based labour status should not be treated as substitutes.

measurement_notes.question: Bahraini or non-Bahraini workforce?
measurement_notes.answer: Nationality is a major labour-market dimension. Total employment can move differently from Bahraini employment.

measurement_notes.question: Which CBB rate?
measurement_notes.answer: CBB monetary facilities have instrument-specific rates. The page requires the exact facility and decision date rather than a generic 'policy rate' field.

measurement_notes.question: Does Bahrain's dollar peg erase domestic credit conditions?
measurement_notes.answer: No. The peg shapes monetary policy, but bank liquidity, credit demand and domestic spreads remain separate measurable channels.

findings.title: Freshness is a statistical property, not a website-layout property.

findings.title: Administrative employment and unemployment are not inverse measures.

findings.why: Mixing the two constructs can manufacture false labour-market improvement or deterioration.

measurement_notes.question: What is 'the Kuwait policy rate'?
measurement_notes.answer: Under-specified. CBK publishes a discount rate plus repo rates at multiple tenors. The instrument must be named before comparison.

measurement_notes.question: Is the dinar pegged to the US dollar?
measurement_notes.answer: Not directly. CBK states that the KWD exchange rate is linked to a special weighted basket of currencies reflecting major trade and financial partners.

measurement_notes.question: Can overnight and one-month repo rates be plotted as one continuous series?
measurement_notes.answer: Only if tenor changes are explicitly modeled. They are different instruments, not missing versions of the same observation.

measurement_notes.question: Kuwaiti unemployment or total unemployment?
measurement_notes.answer: Nationality is a key perimeter in Kuwait's labour market. A total rate may answer a different policy question from a citizens-only rate.

measurement_notes.question: Does total GDP tell the same story as non-oil activity?
measurement_notes.answer: No. Hydrocarbon production can dominate aggregate output changes, so oil and non-oil components should be preserved separately.

findings.title: Kuwait's monetary stance cannot be represented by one unnamed rate.
findings.body: CBK currently publishes a 3.50% discount rate alongside repo rates of 3.625% overnight, 3.875% at one week and 4.125% at one month.
findings.why: Selecting one without instrument metadata can fabricate cross-country spreads or false policy changes.

findings.why: Regional labels should not replace country-specific exchange-rate institutions.

findings.title: A city-level inflation series can become a fake national series in one missing word.

findings.why: This prevents official-rate data from being misused as evidence about a market it does not measure.
